◆ MakeBotPoseType

enum class superdex::robotics::MakeBotPoseType
strong

The kind of pose MakeBotPose should produce.

Enumerator
Zero 

All DOFs set to 0, then clamped to the joint's limits if present.

Min 

minLimit when present; otherwise the Random-fallback low (revolute/spherical 0, prismatic -1).

Max 

maxLimit when present; otherwise the Random-fallback high (revolute/spherical 2pi, prismatic +1).

Mid 

Midpoint (lo+hi)/2 when both limits exist; otherwise 0 clamped to whichever side exists.

Random 

Uniform sample within [lo, hi]; fallback range when a limit is missing is [0, 2pi] for Revolute/Spherical and [-1, +1] for Prismatic.

◆ ArchiveBot()

void superdex::robotics::ArchiveBot ( ArchiveParams const & params,
superdex::Error & error )

Archive a .superdex_bot file and all its transitive dependencies into a self-contained .superdex_bot_archive zip file.

Recursively collects every referenced file — other .superdex_bot files (ModBotPrefab::base, AttachBot::path, ReplaceLinkWithBot::path) and model assets (shapeFile, renderModelFile) — then compresses them into a single zip file at the destination.

The archive mirrors the on-disk multi-root topology rooted at the deepest common ancestor of all involved .superdex_root directories: each source root is laid out at its relative offset under the archive top, and one (possibly rewritten) .superdex_root file is included per source root. Tags whose target is not in the archive are dropped; surviving tags are rewritten to the relative path between the archived roots so cross-root @tag references continue to resolve.

Errors out if the involved .superdex_root directories share no common ancestor (e.g. different Windows drive letters). The destination path must end with .superdex_bot_archive.

Parameters
[in]paramsArchive parameters (source bot, destination .superdex_bot_archive path).

◆ BuildArticulatedPoseFromBotPose()

DynamicArray< real > superdex::robotics::BuildArticulatedPoseFromBotPose ( BotPrefab const & botPrefab,
Span< real const > srcPose,
int numActorDofs,
superdex::Error & error )
nodiscard

Convert a bot-space pose to an articulated-actor pose.

Bot DOFs never include the root joint's, whether or not the articulation has any: a Free root contributes 6 actor DOFs that bot space excludes, and a Hard root contributes none. The two spaces therefore share an order and differ only by that leading offset, so this copies srcPose to pose[i + numBaseDofs] and zero-fills the base DOFs, producing the actor-DOF layout Actor::SetArticulatedPoseFromJoints expects. It never permutes.

Parameters
[in]botPrefabBot describing the articulation.
[in]srcPoseBot-space pose (must have one entry per bot-space DOF).

Returns
Pose in actor-DOF layout, sized to numActorDofs.

◆ FindAssetBaseFolder()

std::filesystem::path superdex::robotics::FindAssetBaseFolder ( std::filesystem::path const & originDir)
nodiscard

Resolve the base folder of the asset that originDir belongs to.

Ascends to the nearest role-folder ancestor (IsAssetRoleSubdirName) and resolves to its parent; a path with no role folder above it resolves to itself. Nothing on disk is consulted.

This anchors lookups and default save paths on the asset itself rather than on a fixed number of directory levels. Counting levels breaks on a flat asset, where it reaches past the asset into the folder holding its siblings – a namespace shared with unrelated assets. Ascending rather than checking only the immediate name additionally handles a role folder partitioned into subfolders, e.g. cad/internal/ holding CAD sources that must not be open-sourced.

Warning
Being purely lexical, this treats any role-folder name on the way up as the asset's, so an asset nested beneath a folder that happens to be named cad / render / collision / intermediates anchors one level too high. No asset in the tree is laid out that way.
Parameters
[in]originDirDirectory holding the file being worked on.
Returns
The asset's base folder.

◆ NormalizeBotPath()

std::filesystem::path superdex::robotics::NormalizeBotPath ( std::filesystem::path const & path)
nodiscard

Absolute + lexically normalized, with any trailing separator dropped.

The single definition of what a bot path means, used wherever one is resolved, compared or collected. Symlinks are deliberately NOT resolved: an asset tree can be a symlink farm (buck-out file groups are), and resolving would place a file that exists in the link's target tree while a file the build does not have – which a bot may legitimately name – has no link to follow and stays where it was written. The two then have no relative form between them. Treating paths as written keeps every reference in one tree, at the cost of not recognising two spellings of one file as the same; an archive then carries such a file at both paths, which is what its references require.

Parameters
[in]pathPath to normalize; may name a file that does not exist.

◆ ParseRootFile()

ParsedRootFile superdex::robotics::ParseRootFile ( std::filesystem::path const & rootFilePath,
superdex::Error & error )
nodiscard

Parse a .superdex_root JSON file into its tag table.

The file is a JSON object mapping "@tagName" keys to path strings. Empty or whitespace-only files are valid and produce an empty tag table. Relative tag values are resolved against the directory containing the .superdex_root file, then weakly_canonical-ized. Each resolved tag directory is verified to itself contain a .superdex_root marker.

Any invalid entry (malformed key, key not matching the kTagPrefix identifier rules, or target directory missing a .superdex_root marker) is treated as a hard error: the function logs the offending entry and returns failure with no tags loaded.

Parameters
[in]rootFilePathPath to the .superdex_root file.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
Parsed tag table on success, default-constructed on failure.

◆ ResolveBotPath()

std::filesystem::path superdex::robotics::ResolveBotPath ( std::string_view input,
std::filesystem::path const & basePath,
int maxParentDepth,
superdex::Error & error )
nodiscard

Resolve a bot path string into an absolute path.

The single source of truth for path resolution rules used by all bot file references:

  • Empty input -> empty result.
  • A file-relative input may ascend at most maxParentDepth parent (..) directories; more than that -> hard error. @tag/... and //... remainders are always descendant-only (any .. -> hard error), regardless of maxParentDepth.
  • Absolute input -> hard error (absolute bot paths are not allowed).
  • @tag/... -> look up @tag in the nearest .superdex_root tag table (walking up from basePath) and join the remainder.
  • //... -> resolve against the directory of the nearest .superdex_root marker (regardless of its tag table).
  • Anything else -> join with basePath.parent_path() and weakly_canonical.
Parameters
[in]inputRaw path string (e.g. from a .superdex_bot or .mochi_bot_scene field).
[in]basePathThe referencing file (its parent directory is used as the search/join origin).
[in]maxParentDepthMaximum number of parent (..) directories a file-relative path may ascend. Pass 0 for descendant-only, which all bot references use. Callers that store loosely-coupled local clusters (e.g. Studio's .StudioProcessing.json) may pass a small positive value. No default: every caller must state its policy explicitly.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
Absolute resolved path.

◆ SafeDot()

real superdex::robotics::SafeDot ( Real3 const & a,
Real3 const & b )
nodiscard

Dot product that treats 0 * inf as 0, avoiding IEEE 754 NaN.

Standard Dot produces NaN when one operand has ±inf in a component where the other operand is zero (e.g. Dot({-inf, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 1}) = NaN + 0 + 0 = NaN). This variant skips terms where either factor is zero.

Parameters
[in]aFirst operand.
[in]bSecond operand.
Returns
Dot product with 0 * inf treated as 0.

void superdex::robotics::SortBotPrefab ( BotPrefab & botPrefab,
superdex::Error & error )

Sort bot link/joint/defaultPose data so that children follow their parents and siblings are ordered by alphanumeric (natural) comparison of link names.

Performs a DFS pre-order traversal of the link tree, visiting siblings in alphanumeric order. The resulting permutation is applied to BotPrefab::links, BotPrefab::joints, and BotPrefab::defaultPose. Does NOT recompute internal fields; the caller should follow with a call to RebuildBotData.

Note
Called automatically by RebuildBotData.
Parameters
[in,out]botPrefabBot parameters to sort (modified in place).

◆ UnresolveBotPath()

DynamicString superdex::robotics::UnresolveBotPath ( std::filesystem::path const & absPath,
std::filesystem::path const & basePath,
int maxParentDepth,
superdex::Error & error )
nodiscard

Convert an absolute path to its canonical bot-path string form for serialization.

This is the inverse of ResolveBotPath.

The result is always a valid ResolveBotPath input that resolves to the same absolute path. It is not guaranteed to be string-identical to the original input, because multiple input forms may refer to the same path and this function deterministically selects the highest-priority form per the rules below. For example, an input @assets/foo whose target is also reachable via // will round-trip as //foo.

Selection rules, applied in order:

  1. File-relative — if absPath is reachable from basePath.parent_path() while ascending at most maxParentDepth parent (..) directories, emit that relative form. With the default maxParentDepth of 0 this is a plain descendant, as all bot references require.
  2. //root-prefixed — else, if absPath is a descendant of FindBotsRoot(basePath), emit //+remainder (always descendant-only).
  3. @tag/... — else, parse the nearest .superdex_root tag table and pick the tag whose target directory is the deepest (most path components) strict ancestor of absPath; ties are broken by lexicographically smallest tag name; emit @tag/+remainder (always descendant-only).

If none of the above produce a valid relative form, the function reports a hard error: absolute bot paths are not permitted on either end of resolution.

Empty input -> empty result. Already-relative input is returned unchanged (defensive; should not happen post-load).

Parameters
[in]absPathAbsolute path to convert.
[in]basePathThe referencing file (its parent directory and bots-root context determine the chosen prefix form).
[in]maxParentDepthMaximum number of parent (..) directories the file-relative form (rule 1) may ascend before falling back to // / @tag. Pass 0 for descendant-only, which all bot references use. The // and @tag forms are unaffected and stay descendant-only. No default: every caller must state its policy explicitly.
[in,out]errorError status. Check Error::IsOK for success.
Returns
Canonical string representation acceptable as ResolveBotPath input.
